newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - June 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - June 3.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- Foreign capital poured into Sout Africa at an unprecedented rate in May, lifting the Reserve Bank's gold and foreign exchange reserves a massive 7.4 billion rand to a record 21.8 billion rand.
- The battle between two Tollgate liquidators and Absa over the validity of Absa's 246 million rand claim against Kyalami International Circuit has been taken to the Cape High Court.

- The Congress of SA Trade Unions' 24-hour strike on Monday in support of better working conditions, which caused the loss of millions of rands to the economy, could be repeated soon if business did not heed worker demands, Cosatu leaders said at courtrywide marches.
- A tender issued by Telkom for creating a value-added network worth more than 100 million rand has been halted amid allegations that the tender was biased towards a specific vendor.

- World Cup rugby stars Hennie le Roux and Kobus Wiese were axed from the Springbok squad to face Tonga and the British Lions, but new coach Carel du Plessis denied there had been any instructions for him to drop them.
BUSINESS REPORT

- Customs was powerless to act against companies that had smuggled millions of rands worth of branded electronics goods into South Africa because members of the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA) were withholding critical information from investigators, sources said last week.

- Business should settle its disputes with labour in Nedlac otherwise Cosatu would simply use its relationship with the ANC to push its demands through parliament, Sam Shilowa, the general secretary of Cosatu, warned on Monday.

- Dorbyl, the industrial and engineering company, will close its bus plant in the Eastern Cape by the end of next month and relocate to India, Rob Duff, the transport division managing director, said on Monday.

- Saflife and newly acquired NK Properties, which is being used as a vehicle for Mzi Khumalo and Brett Kebble to control JCI, are to merge, creating a four billion rand gold focused investment group, industry sources said on Monday.
- Rand Merchant Bank (RMB) plans to launch a new banking division for wealthy individuals, as opposed to corporate customers, the bank announced on Monday.
- The new government in the former Zaire has opened the door for Spoornet to return to the central African country after officials admitted that nationalising the railroads was a mistake.
SAKE BEELD
- South Africa's foreign reserve rose from the previous month by 7.4 billion rand to 21,8 billion rand.
- Cosatu said that is was pleased with the outcome of its one-day strike on Monday.
THE STAR
- Business and the labour movement are at odds over the success of Monday's strike called by Cosatu to protest against provisions of the Basic Conditions of Employment Draft Bill.
- Three people died and nine were badly hurt when a Translux bus crashed on the N3 near Villiers in the Free State on Monday.
